analysis.title: BofA on USA: Weekly spending update through Oct 24
key_insights: Total card spending per household rose 6.0% y/y in the week ending Oct 24, per BAC aggregated credit and debit card data, up from 4.9% on Oct 17.
Total card spending excluding gas rose 4.8% y/y in the week ending Oct 24, up from 3.7% on Oct 17. Gas spending was up 25.5% y/y, which accounts for the gap between the two measures.
Spending growth strengthened broadly relative to the prior week, led by entertainment, clothing and online retail.
Entertainment spending growth moved from -4.3% y/y on Oct 17 to +6.9% on Oct 24. Clothing moved from 0.1% to 3.4%. Total online retail moved from 5.0% to 8.3%.
Lower-income spending growth has consistently outpaced higher-income spending growth over the past several weeks (total card ex gas per household, by income tercile).
Retail ex-autos was up 5.3% y/y on Oct 24 (3.8% on Oct 17). Total brick-and-mortar retail was up 3.8% and total online retail was up 8.3%.
Airlines spending growth was 8.3% y/y on Oct 24, down from 9.1% on Oct 17. Lodging was up 1.7% and restaurants and bars were up 3.8%.
Weak categories on Oct 24: furniture -5.3% y/y, department stores -2.2%, grocery -0.5%. Home improvement was up 1.7% and general merchandise up 5.4%.

macro_indicators.indicator: BAC total card spending per household (y/y, 7-day MA)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Consumer card spending growth strengthened over the week, though gas price inflation contributes to the headline.

macro_indicators.indicator: BAC total card spending ex gas per household (y/y, 7-day MA)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Excluding gas, growth is about 1.2 points lower than the headline.
Gas spending growth has stayed between about 25% and 27% across the week, which inflates the headline total.

risk_factors: BAC card data covers debit and credit cards only, excludes cash, checks and ACH payments, and may reflect selection bias in income levels and geographies.
charts_described: Exhibit 2 plots total card, retail ex auto and total card ex gas spending per household, y/y, from Oct-25 to Oct-26, with the text stating ex-gas spending was up 4.8% y/y in the week ending Oct 24.

Exhibit 3 plots total card ex gas spending per household by lower and higher income group, y/y, from Oct 25 to Oct 26, with the text stating lower-income growth has consistently outpaced higher-income growth over the past several weeks.
